sub1: Weekday Lates with weeks 14–17 kept in order and ON THEIR OWN LINES, week 13 moved away, and the evening gap filled
eyebrow3: Weekday Lates, weeks 14–17 held in place
h3: What was held, what moved, and what it cost
sub3: Four of the five protected weeks never move at all; one does, and that is what makes the rest work
coverNote: gaps of 8, 6, 5, 5 around the wheel — inherited from Weekday Lates, not re-spread
h7: How it was built, and how to load it
sub7: Reproducible: the same starting grid, seed and objective give the same rotation on any machine
method:
1 · Weeks 14, 15, 16 and 17 do not move. They sit at lines 14, 15, 16 and 17, in that order, exactly as written in Weekday Lates — not a day, not a time, not a line number altered. That is the difference between this proposal and Weekday Lates 3, which kept the same five weeks to the letter but scattered them to lines 21, 3, 6, 24 and 1.

2 · Week 13 moves, and only week 13. It keeps its duties exactly as written and goes to line 4. It has to move, and the reason is arithmetic rather than preference: week 13 works Tue–Sat and week 14 Sun–Mon, so back to back they are seven consecutive working days totalling 58.9 hours against MRSF's 55-hour limit. That window lies wholly inside those two weeks, so no rearrangement of the other twenty-two can break it. Separated, the worst seven-day window is 54.7h and the row clears.

3 · The block's position was enumerated, not searched. Cover weeks are pinned at 1, 7, 12 and 17, and week 17 is one of them — a cover week is blank, so “14, 15, 16, 17 in order” means the three working weeks sitting immediately before some cover week. On a 24-line wheel that is four placements and no more, so all four were tried at three seeds each. Twelve runs, every one clearing every threshold; the placement that keeps the weeks on their own line numbers is the one printed here.

4 · Then the rest of the wheel was searched fatigue-first. Every factor present charged over and above its size, three restarts a seed, with only the two coverage-preserving moves — so the cover curve is identical to Weekday Lates 3's, hour for hour, and the ordering choice costs nothing in cover.
openQuestions: The seven-day run is the price, and it is structural. The longest working stretch is 7 days against Weekday Lates 3's 6. Week 14 works Fri–Sat and week 15 Sun–Thu, so holding those two in order is seven straight days whatever else moves. It is not a threshold breach — FF11 allows 13 consecutive and the “more than 7 consecutive 8h shifts” row needs more than seven — but 6 is what the other proposals reach, and this one cannot. What holding the line numbers cost. Of the twelve runs, one placement reached 7 full weekends off against this design's 6 — but it puts the block on lines 22, 23 and 24 instead of 14, 15 and 16. That candidate is in the table opposite: a weekend against the line numbers, and it is the room's call rather than the search's. FF19 is at its floor. Two instances of successive start times varying by more than two hours, down from Weekday Lates 3's three. No rotation holding both early and late weeks can reach zero — crossing from earlies to lates is by definition a jump over two hours — and two is the arithmetic floor for this mix of turns, which Weekday Lates 3's own notes state. Weeks 13–17 in full. If all five must stay in order, MRSF is present at 58.9h and the floor is two factors rather than one; that is a property of the 13→14 join, not a limit of the search.
